subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw ship default-on automatic subagent inactivity recovery, and should the first supported policy be nudge-then-kill, kill-only, alert-only, or split across the session activity watchdog and subagent registry?
rationale: The source problem is real, but the requested behavior changes default runtime policy, config shape, parent notification semantics, and session-kill behavior for existing deployments.

options.title: Keep canonical design issue
options.body: Keep this issue open as the owner-visible design item for automatic subagent stall recovery while related pieces land separately.

options.title: Prioritize manual recovery first
options.body: Defer automatic nudge/kill and land the manual kill/reap escape hatch before adding default-on policy.

options.title: Route through activity watchdog
options.body: Make this dependent on the broader session activity API/watchdog instead of adding a subagent-specific inactivity loop now.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical design issue
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the owner-visible design item for automatic subagent stall recovery while related pieces land separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame owns the central subagent registry, control, and config paths where this policy would land.
